title: Cap. 6 Arg. 6: Aquinas—saving gifts rest on simple divine will; prevenience for some who block grace
pass_a_gloss: Finally Aquinas himself thinks no other reason ought to be given why the gifts of saving grace are given to these particular persons, and are not given to others, besides the simple will of God (Contra Gentiles, book 3, chapter 161). "Although," he says, "he who sins presents an impediment to grace, and insofar as the order of things requires he ought not to receive grace, yet sometimes, from the abundance of his goodness, he also prevents with his help those who present an impediment to grace, turning them from evil and converting them to good," and so on. Soon he adds: "He does not prevent with his help all who impede grace, but some in whom he wills his mercy to appear, so that in others the order of justice may be manifested."
pass_b_english: Aquinas too will give no other reason why these particular persons receive the gifts of saving grace, and others do not, than the simple will of God (Contra Gentiles 3.161). "Though the sinner," he says, "puts an obstacle in grace's way, and so far as the order of things requires ought not to receive grace, yet sometimes, from the abundance of his goodness, God also goes before with his help even those who put that obstacle there, turning them from evil and converting them to good," and the rest. He adds at once: "He does not go before with his help all who block grace, but some in whom he wills his mercy to appear, so that in others the order of justice may be shown."
source_text: Denique ipse Aquinas non aliam rationem reddendam putat, cur hisce singularibus personis dentur gratiae salutiferae dona, aliis non dentur, praeter simplicem Dei voluntatem; Contr. Gent. lib. 3. cap. 161. Licet, inquit, ille qui peccat, impedimentum gratiae praestet, & in quantum ordo rerum exigit gratiam non deberet recipere, tamen interdum, ex abundantia bonitatis suae, etiam eos qui impedimentum gratiae praestant, auxilio suo praevenit, avertens eos a malo, & convertens ad bonum, &c. Mox addit, Non omnes qui gratiam impediunt auxilio suo praevenit, sed aliquos in quibus vult misericordiam suam apparere, ita quod in aliis justitiae ordo manifestetur.
